intro.title: Test User Interactions
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive React component with a button that increments a counter when clicked. You will learn how to test user interactions by simulating button clicks and verifying that the counter updates correctly. The main technologies involved are React for the component, JavaScript for the logic, and React Testing Library for writing the tests. This will help you understand how to ensure your components respond properly to user actions.
intro.usecase: Testing user interactions is essential for ensuring that interactive UI components work correctly in production applications. Developers use these tests to verify that form submissions, button clicks, dropdown selections, and modal dialogs behave as expected in e-commerce checkouts, dashboard controls, and data filtering interfaces. This practice prevents bugs in critical user flows like login authentication, shopping cart updates, and settings configuration panels. By writing interaction tests, developers can confidently deploy features that users rely on daily while maintaining application stability.
